changes.after: El-Ahsa: Dünyanın en büyük vahasını bölüm bölüm keşfedin
changes.why: H13-r3: third reader on the H1 (on-05 "literary", on-r1 "stiff", on-r2 "sounds translated"); the threshold is met, so the text changes. «önünüze seriliyor» is the stumbling verb; «keşfedin» is the plain Turkish site verb, siz form, no fact added. «bölüm bölüm» stays: it carries "chapter by chapter" (the seven chapters, rail.label «Sayfanın bölümleri»), so the reader's doubt (page sections or parts of the oasis?) resolves to both, which is what the source means. The reader's «adım adım» drops the chapter link and is not taken. Fixed phrase «dünyanın en büyük vaha-» unchanged (C15). Capital after the colon: a full sentence follows.

changes.before: Suudi Arabistan'ın Doğu Bölgesi'nde: kumun altında su, mağaralarla dolu bir dağ ve nesillerdir yaşayan çarşılar. El-Ahsa'da gezilecek yerler ve yapılacaklar için rehberiniz burada. Başlamak için sayfayı kaydırın.
changes.after: Suudi Arabistan'ın Doğu Bölgesi'nde: kumun altında su, mağaralarla dolu bir dağ ve nesillerdir süregelen çarşılar. El-Ahsa'da gezilecek yerler ve yapılacaklar için rehberiniz burada. Başlamak için sayfayı kaydırın.
changes.why: H7-r3: third reader on the generations phrase in a third form («yaşayan» = markets that "live", foreign). «nesillerdir süregelen» is the third reader's own proposal: «süregelen» = continuing from the past to now (TDK süregelmek), the usual collocation for traditions and markets; «nesillerdir» answers the second reader (who stumbled on «kuşaklardır»). Final form; declared source shape (closed in the addendum). Same words as memory.lead. No age claim.

A6-ministry (tr-attr-6) writes «Suudi Arabistan'ın Çevre, Su ve Tarım Bakanlığı» at first mention; the sources line is the ministry's only mention on this page and it is read as text, not as a bibliographic entry, so A6 applies. The country adds no fact (the ministry is the Saudi one) and disambiguates as A4-Dogu-Bolgesi allows. Edge spaces and the other pieces unchanged.

H4-r3: third reader on «Kuşluk» (on-05 "bookish", on-r1 "may not be understood", on-r2 "prayer-time words next to plain words"). The threshold is met, so the ticks change to one plain register: «Şafak · Sabah · Öğleden sonra · Gün batımı» = the English (Morning, Afternoon) and the published ru precedent «Рассвет · Утро · После полудня · Закат». The ctx's guard holds: «Öğleden sonra» does not read as evening or dusk (tick 4 is sunset). Loss logged: the Arabic's precision (الضحى mid-morning) is no longer carried; «Sabah» is the English word.

H4-r3: as qarah.time.morning; «İkindi» was the second prayer-time word the third reader named. Two words like ru «После полудня»; the tick row wraps (flex-wrap) and the published de row («Morgengrauen · Vormittag · Spätnachmittag · Sonnenuntergang») is longer.

rulings.title: Chapter names in the rail and eyebrows
rulings.ruling: The seven names: «Giriş» · «Kumun altındaki su» · «Cebel el-Kare» · «Etkileşimli harita» · «Toprağın ve çarşının hafızası» · «Gezinizi planlayın» · «Kapanış». "The Gate" = «Giriş» (not «Kapı», not «Açılış»). Each works bare in the rail/aria-label and as «0N · <name>».
rulings.evidence: Reader p1#2, labels#5 (bare «Kapı» = stray door); Giriş/Kapanış is the ordinary Turkish opening/closing pair; zh 入口.

rulings.title: Number cards and their four labels
rulings.ruling: Plus shape kept for both counted numbers («2,5 milyon+», «280+»). Labels: «hurma ağacı — dünyanın en büyük vahası» · «artezyen pınar vahayı sular» (pınar = the site's spring word) · «UNESCO Dünya Mirası Listesi'ne alındığı yıl» (nominal under the year) · «keşfedilecek yer» (one noun for one count).
rulings.evidence: ChapterWater.astro: .wf-n up to 3.2rem in a 4-column grid; the word form would wrap where the de/ru words do not; the count-up regex /\d+(?:[.,]\d+)?/ handles «2,5». Reader p1#6-8.

rulings.title: Chapter 3 heading
rulings.ruling: «Cebel el-Kare: Günün saatini siz seçin» — names the action the slider performs, echoes the slider label «Günün saati»; capital after the colon (full sentence).
rulings.evidence: English "move the day yourself", Arabic «حرّك اليوم بيدك»; reader p1#9; stage 3 rejected «ilerletin» (forward only).

rulings.title: The four ticks
rulings.ruling: «Şafak · Kuşluk · İkindi · Gün batımı» kept. Logged for calibration: if a second reader stumbles on «Kuşluk», the only candidate that keeps the arbiter is «Kuşluk vakti» on the tick with the others unchanged — not «Sabah».
rulings.evidence: Arabic arbiter (الفجر · الضحى · الأصيل · الغروب, ctx); TDK kuşluk "sabah ile öğle arası"; one reader, a register remark, no misreading.

rulings.title: Chapter 4 name and the map aria-label

rulings.evidence: Reader p1#11, labels#1; zh/de/ru "interactive".

rulings.evidence: Two readers on two forms (on-05 #4, on-r1 #4/#22); Arabic «تعاقبت عليها الأجيال»; «yaşayan tarihî çarşı» usage.

rulings.title: "clay" in editorial headings and leads: scope for the termbase (amends H8)
rulings.ruling: Scope: (a) English "clay" / Arabic الطين in an editorial heading or lead (home chapter 5, any later page hero/lead) → «toprak»: heading «Toprağın ve çarşının hafızası» (rail.ch-memory = memory.title), lead attributive «Toprak kaleler» (not «Topraktan kaleler» — the «kumdan kale» sandcastle pattern). (b) "mud" in factual bodies and summaries → «çamur» (A2-wording, tr-attr-1, unchanged). (c) «kerpiç» only where the English says "mud brick" (tm Muheyris body). A later batch must not turn (a) into «çamur» or «kerpiç», nor (b) into «toprak».

The English names two landmarks (Jabal Al-Qarah to Qaisariyah Souq) and "maps, events and itineraries"; the Arabic names four (adds Qasr Ibrahim and Al-Uqair) and adds restaurants. The ctx says the Arabic lists the same four — the English does not. Turkish follows the English.
English "Plan your visit" vs. nav "Plan your trip" for the same target; Turkish uses the approved «Gezinizi planlayın» for both.
The English promises "events"; the home page links events only through the header (reader p1#1).

«Hüfuf», «Uyuniler Devleti», «Cebel el-Erba» and the national park are termbase/published names the English does not gloss (A5); «Hofuf's fortresses» plural and «the eastern villages» are the English's (routes#1, #2, #5; companion#2).
Same final stop (Ukayr Kıyı Rotası) described two ways by the English (routes#7).
El-Kaysariye is a stop of Tarihî Hüfuf Rotası, the pottery a stop inside Cebel el-Kare ve Cüvasa Rotası; neither is visible in the route list (routes#8, #9).
The English gives no reason the museum is the solo suggestion (companion#3).
The English names no country for the ministry (on-r1 #9, on-r2 #5); the Turkish now carries «Suudi Arabistan'ın» (A6-ministry, H17-r3), no fact added.

Declared source shape in round 3 (closed): "souqs passed down through generations", "Memory of clay and souq" and "life thrives" are the owner's literary images; each drew two or three readers on successive forms.

owner_questions: The map prints «N ↑» in every language; a Turkish map shows «K». Localise the compass letter per language?

The El-Asfar Gölü summary (English: "one of the largest bodies of water in the Arabian Gulf region") read as comparing the lake with the Gulf itself; is "largest inland water bodies" or "largest lakes" what the source means? Only the English can change.
Ukayr sits under the chapter 5 heading "Memory of clay and souq" — keep the card set, or move/replace it?
The 4x4 note prints after the whole three-day nature route (after Ukayr); print it under day 2 (the lake)?
One-day plans print «Birinci gün» with no second day; drop the day heading on one-day routes?
Memory cards carry dates on two landmarks only; add dates to the other three (owner facts) or keep two?

The count-up on the two number cards paints intermediate values with the final suffix: measured on «280'den fazla», the slow tail (last ~0.5 s of 1.8 s, values 272-279) shows «273'den», «275'den», «276'den», «279'den» — wrong Turkish harmony. «2,5 milyondan fazla» is safe (the suffix sits on «milyon»). Fix in ChapterWater.astro: paint only before + digits during the count (or hide the suffix) and restore the full text at the end, as the script already does on the last frame — or keep?
Six identical «Kaydedildi ✓» states: put the place name into the saved state's accessible label?

Two Turkish readers find the published «Duvarları çamurdan» (Kasr İbrahim) crude and the El-Kaysariye summary's «İki yüzyıldan eski» odd; a summary revision would be a separate batch (A2-wording binds «çamur» for "mud").

The Cebel el-Kare slider ticks now read «Şafak · Sabah · Öğleden sonra · Gün batımı» (three readers on «Kuşluk»/«İkindi»); the Arabic's mid-morning / late-afternoon precision is no longer carried. Acceptable, or do you want the precise prayer-time words back?

The sources line now says «Suudi Arabistan'ın Çevre, Su ve Tarım Bakanlığı» (two readers asked which country); the English says only "Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture". Add the country to the English too?
